# 通膨降溫支持短債，長端融資成本仍居高不下

## CPI讓Fed多些等待空間，長債卻未受惠

7月通膨報告讓Fed有更多時間觀察，卻未替長期借款人帶來多少成本減輕。2年期美債殖利率下跌2個基點至4.20%，10年期同樣跌2個基點至4.68%，30年期則維持5.24%。市場對9月升息的定價由約50%降至40%，但年底前升息一次仍已完全反映在價格中。

整體CPI月增0.1%、年增3.4%，年增率由3.5%回落；核心物價月增0.2%、年增2.5%，年增率也由2.6%下降。四項數據均符合預期。能源降價與溫和的居住成本有所幫助，但租金仍在上漲，資料中心熱潮也推高部分電腦相關價格。10年期實質殖利率與損益兩平通膨率各降1個基點，分別收在2.42%及2.26%。

$420億10年期美債標售以4.683%得標，為2007年以來最高，且略高於標售前市場水準。新增供給獲得消化，未引發劇烈波動，但有利的通膨數據也沒讓投資人追買長債。30年期殖利率不動，使2年與30年期利差擴大2個基點至104個基點；近一個月30年期殖利率仍上升18個基點，2年期則下降1個基點。

股市歡迎Fed可暫待觀察，由科技股領漲。信用市場也持續提供融資：Jane Street發行$146億擔保債券，最長年期殖利率達8.088%。The Knot與波羅的海航空（Air Baltic）的條件卻嚴苛得多，前者須支付更高利息，後者債權人面臨大幅損失。CPI減輕了一項壓力，長期資金與弱體質借款人的融資成本仍然高昂。

## 通膨放緩之下，租金與科技產品仍有漲價壓力

7月整體CPI小幅上升，前一個月則下跌0.4%。核心月增率由持平回升至0.2%，年增率卻追平2021年3月以來最低。能源價格下跌1.5%，居住成本僅上漲0.1%，但仍貢獻整體月增幅約三分之二。旅館與汽車旅館降價壓低居住成本，兩項主要租金指標卻都上漲0.3%。

扣除能源與租金的服務價格在6月下跌後回升0.2%，醫療照護與機票都在上漲項目之列。扣除食品與能源的商品價格也在連跌兩個月後反彈。電腦軟體及配件年漲21.2%、創紀錄，其他電腦相關項目的漲幅亦為四年多來最大，背景是記憶體晶片短缺與資料中心建設需求。整體通膨雖降溫，內部並非全面疲弱。

家庭購買力也未增強。實質平均時薪年減0.2%，延續伊朗衝突爆發以來的疲弱表現。這與招聘降溫一起，讓Fed即使面對高於2%的整體通膨，也有理由不急著再升息。不過，租金黏性與7月會議的三張反對票，使後續緊縮仍有可能。市場減少的是部分9月升息風險，而非撤去年底前升息的預期。

5年期殖利率下跌1個基點至4.38%。2年期已回到接近8月7日非農公布後的水準，5年與10年期卻仍高於當時。10年期實質殖利率與通膨補償各降1個基點，也不同於週二完全由通膨補償帶動的漲勢。近一個月實質殖利率仍升10個基點，損益兩平通膨率升2個基點，先前累積的融資成本上升大多尚未消退。

2年與10年期殖利率降幅相同，利差維持48個基點；近一個月這段曲線已轉陡13個基點，2年與30年期利差則擴大19個基點，顯示長端得到的舒緩少得多。10年期殖利率同期仍高12個基點。赤字、供給與買方結構的不確定性，並未因一次通膨報告而消失。

收盤變動雖小，交易並不清淡。名目附息公債按原始面額計算的成交額增加19.7%至$9,461億。2年及以下天期增加33.4%，7年至10年期增加30.9%，成交增量集中在對CPI敏感的短債與當日標售附近的年期。10年期標售的小幅讓利是在活躍市場中形成；週四30年期債券的存續期間曝險更大，仍須另行檢驗其買方需求。

## Jane Street籌得$146億，弱體質企業付出更高展期代價

美債上漲、風險偏好增強，LQD上漲0.12%，HYG與JNK分別漲0.13%及0.17%。個別交易則呈現更完整的融資面貌，從大額擔保發行，到重整中債權人的損失，條件差異鮮明。

Jane Street發行約$146億優先擔保債券，分別為2031年到期的$58.6億、2033年到期的$51.3億及2036年到期的$36.4億，最長年期殖利率為8.088%。資金將用於$110億債務調整方案中的浮動利率貸款再融資，並支持科技基礎設施與新交易策略。前一年創紀錄的$396億交易收入有助支撐發行，但投資人對最長年期仍要求8%以上殖利率。

評等也反映其高獲利與資產負債表透明度有限並存的特性。標普給予債券BB、較投資級低兩級；惠譽的發行人評等則為最低投資級BBB-。擔保地位與獲利能力支持大額籌資，但能為再融資與科技投資取得資金，不代表資金便宜。

QTS子公司開始與投資人溝通一筆可能約$28.5億、亦可能增額的發行案，預計取得投資級評等。融資涉及黑石支持、出租給微軟的喬治亞州開發案；此前曾討論$54億債券與貸款方案，7月另有以Project Magnolia支持的$32.5億槓桿貸款。本次仍在行銷階段，尚未完成發行，資料中心供給則持續透過專案融資與資產擔保渠道增加。

上海電氣重新打開一條管制較嚴的融資渠道。這家上海市支持的設備製造商，在上海自貿區發行CNY15億3年期綠色票據，利率由初步討論約2.4%收窄至1.8%。這是2023年底主管機關限制地方政府借款後，首家在該市場完成定價的非金融企業，也是公司2020年以來首次境外發行。香港子公司保證、維好協議及A3評等支持需求；受惠的是具支持架構、信用較好的借款人，並非地方槓桿限制全面鬆綁。

The Knot爭取的展期昂貴得多。公司推出$6.7億貸款，擬將現有$6.6億融資展延2.5年，數小時後穆迪便將評等下調兩級至Caa1。擬議利差由375個基點升至525個基點；若槓桿達EBITDA的4倍以上，另加100個基點，這部分可採利息資本化（PIK）。現有貸款價格已由去年底約面額99%跌至約70%。

公司2025年營收下降2%，2026年預計再減，利潤率維持20%出頭。AI生成的搜尋內容削弱網站流量與商家參與，是營運壓力來源。標普維持B評等，但警告槓桿若高於盈餘7倍可能降評。展延到期日能替公司爭取時間，PIK則可保留現金，代價是在槓桿已高時繼續累積債務。

波羅的海航空的擔保債權人損失更深。€3.8億、2029年到期債券，從重整公布前約面額35%跌至最低12%；交易稀疏，也曾出現20%出頭的報價。航空公司計畫將大部分債券轉為股權，保留€1.25億債務，另籌€2.25億過渡融資，同時縮減機隊與成本。6月償債準備金僅剩€300萬。拉脫維亞政府持有88.4%股權及13%債券，仍未讓債權人免於虧損。

這些企業使用資本市場的目的不同。Jane Street以高票息再融資並擴張，QTS尋找下一筆基礎設施融資，上海電氣進入受管制的境外人民幣市場；The Knot與波羅的海航空則是爭取時間、減輕資產負債表壓力，既有債權人因此承擔更多成本。

## 韓國長債殖利率創高，日本仍在權衡升息速度

韓國30年期公債殖利率升至4.67%，創2012年推出該年期以來最高。進口能源成本與半導體成長可能促使央行進一步緊縮，原已壓抑債市；壽險需求疲弱又讓長端少了一群重要買家。主管機關可能將明年超長債發行比重降至30%以下，但未來供給調整的可能性，尚未阻止當前殖利率創高。

日本政策分歧則繼續影響匯率支撐。美國財長貝森特多次主張，日本銀行收緊政策是穩定日圓的關鍵；首相高市早苗則不願升息太快而傷及成長。她上任後日本銀行已升息兩次，政策利率仍僅1%，美日聯合干預匯率當天也維持不動。日圓再次接近每美元160。

市場預期9月或10月可能升息。生活成本議題升溫，高市支持度下滑；日本銀行官員強調通膨上行風險，內閣成員則持續表態尊重央行獨立性。貝森特預計8月底前後會晤總裁植田和男。政策訊號若更一致，可降低反覆干預的需要；若分歧延續，日本便須繼續在提高國內利率與匯率操作之間權衡。這會影響美債的相對吸引力，但不能據此認定特定外匯存底交易已發生。

能源是兩國共同的外部限制。國際能源署（IEA）目前估計，本季全球供應缺口達每日180萬桶，超過前次預測兩倍，而荷莫茲海峽仍無持久協議。歐洲電價另受高溫帶來的冷氣需求與法國核電減產推升。英國財政部內部模型估計，若海峽實質關閉持續至年底，最壞情境下2026年成長率為0.9%，低於3月預測的1.1%。這是附帶條件的情境分析，不是已實現的成長數據。

即使美國通膨改善，本國殖利率上升仍可能讓海外機構選擇其他資產，而非美元長債。韓國創紀錄的長端殖利率是當前價格訊號，日本下一次升息及干預需求則仍未確定。再加上能源缺口擴大，美國一份有利數據未必能帶動全球債市同步上漲。

## 印尼重新吸引買盤，巴西選舉疑慮侵蝕高息吸引力

美元在CPI公布後先跌後升，收盤上漲0.11%至99.932。新興市場匯率指數回吐盤中最多0.2%的漲幅，紐約收盤大致持平。EMB上漲0.12%，長天期新興市場美元主權債卻僅漲0.04%。9月升息機率下降有助硬通貨債券估值，但不足以壓過各國風險。

南非蘭特隨貴金屬上漲近0.3%，巴西雷亞爾則跌0.3%，韓元跌0.4%。巴西匯率8月至今已跌近2%，選舉疑慮漸增；韓國仍面對能源進口與本地長端殖利率上升的壓力。新興股市同日上漲，也顯示匯率疲弱並非全面風險趨避。

印尼債市開始吸引買家回流，但美元投資人今年仍虧損8.5%、表現居亞洲之末。先前民粹支出、央行獨立性與政府干預疑慮，曾將印尼盾推至歷史低點。Destry Damayanti獲提名出任印尼央行總裁，恢復部分政策延續性；政府計畫縮減免費營養餐方案、維持今年淨發債目標，加上標普確認評等與展望，也有助穩定信心。

基準10年期殖利率已由2022年以來高點回落約27個基點。最新標售的投標額相對目標發行額比率為2月以來最高，外資可望連續第三個月淨流入。下一份預算仍須落實財政約束，央行也須在不犧牲職責的前提下支撐匯率；但改善已有標售需求與外資回流相呼應，不再只是官方表態。

巴西的高利差收益面臨不同考驗。異常高的實質利率支持雷亞爾今年仍上漲約6%，但選舉避險部位不多，當地殖利率上升之際，每週國債標售需求轉弱。抗通膨公債的實質殖利率已超過8%。這既吸引投資人，也提高政府融資負擔；若10月總統選舉前避險需求增強，匯率便可能承壓。

民調顯示總統魯拉領先擴大，市場再次懷疑下一屆政府能否達成足以穩定債務的初級盈餘。部分本地經理人預期短率下降、長率上升，將貨幣寬鬆空間與財政疑慮分開定價。8月匯率下跌與標售疲弱顯示，這些擔憂已在選舉結果揭曉前反映到市場。

新興市場企業債的表現則不同於較脆弱的主權債。廣泛美元企業債指數殖利率8月下降19個基點，美國企業債僅降2個基點，相對借款成本降至1月以來最低。受惠荷莫茲關閉的石油生產商，以及重整取得進展的困境企業領漲。中國萬科2027年到期債在升評後，自6月底累計報酬達30%；Gran Tierra Energy的2031年到期債上漲18%。商品曝險與個別企業復甦，比全面的新興市場行情更能解釋這些漲幅。

## 科技股領漲，黃金仍有避險買盤

S&P 500上漲0.26%，Nasdaq 100上漲0.74%，半導體指數大漲2.49%；VIX下跌4.78%至14.55。股市將CPI解讀為Fed可以等待，而非經濟即將加速惡化，AI熱潮也讓漲勢集中於科技股。

WTI下跌0.90%至$82.45，布蘭特下跌0.66%至$88.32，但近一週仍分別上漲9.61%及11.16%，實際供應尚未恢復正常。美元走強、10年期實質殖利率僅跌1個基點，黃金卻上漲2.52%至$4,493.60。避險需求與風險偏好同時存在，並非單純由美元轉弱帶動。

信用債基金與EMB小幅上漲，新興匯率則失去最初漲勢。對照波羅的海航空的重整損失及The Knot昂貴的再融資條件，市場整體平穩只是背景，不能代表每個借款人的處境。CPI支持估值，卻未消除能源曝險、融資需求或企業營運惡化。

## PPI與長債標售接續檢驗CPI後的行情

7月PPI將於8月13日美東08:30公布。市場共識為月增0.2%，前值月減0.3%，也有月增0.1%的預測。納入核心PCE計算的項目，尤其服務與貿易利潤，將顯示CPI的舒緩是否超越能源降價及暫時性弱項。組合若溫和，可支持Fed耐心及2年至5年期債券；若普遍走強，9月升息敏感度可能回升。Kevin Warsh在8月稍晚的傑克森洞發言，則可看出主席如何解讀陸續累積的證據。

同日$250億30年期標售，面對的是CPI利多後仍停在5.24%的殖利率。相較直接拿10年期得標利率4.683%比較，30年期自己的發行前交易水準、投資人配售與標售後走勢更有意義。若結果平穩且非交易商需求廣泛，表示當前殖利率能吸引長債買家；若得標利率高於發行前水準、交易商承接增加或曲線再度轉陡，便進一步顯示短端舒緩尚未降低長期融資成本。

荷莫茲問題仍待解決。持續通航、各方接受條件、運費與保險成本下降，再加上原油跌至8月12日收盤以下，才足以挑戰IEA擴大的供應缺口估計。若關閉持續或出現新的執法事件，7月CPI能源下跌1.5%便較像對過去的反映，而非持久舒緩的訊號。油價若再漲，損益兩平通膨率與2年期殖利率是否同步上升，將顯示實際供應中斷有多少傳入美國政策定價。
zh-TW.methodology_note: 除另有說明外，市場水準均為紐約收盤值。

overall_summary.headline: 通膨降溫支持短債，長端融資成本仍居高不下
overall_summary.session_narrative:
整體CPI月增0.1%、年增3.4%，核心月增0.2%、年增2.5%。能源降價與溫和的居住成本有所幫助，租金及電腦相關價格卻較強。9月升息機率由約50%降至40%，年底前升息一次仍已完全定價。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
# Softer inflation helps short Treasuries, but leaves the long bond unmoved

## CPI buys the Fed time, not a cheaper long-term borrowing rate

July's inflation report gave the Fed more room to wait, but delivered little relief to long-term borrowers. Two-year Treasury yields fell 2 basis points to 4.20% and ten-year yields declined 2 to 4.68%, while the 30-year stayed at 5.24%. September hike odds slipped to roughly 40% from about 50%; an increase remained fully priced by year-end.

Headline CPI rose 0.1% on the month and 3.4% over a year, down from 3.5%. Core prices increased 0.2% monthly and 2.5% annually, with the annual pace easing from 2.6%. All four readings matched expectations. Cheaper energy and subdued shelter costs helped, although rents continued rising and the data-center boom was pushing up some computer-related prices. At ten years, real yields and breakevens each fell just 1 basis point, to 2.42% and 2.26%.

The $42 billion ten-year auction cleared at 4.683%, the highest yield since 2007 and marginally above the pre-auction level. Buyers absorbed the supply without a disorderly move, but did not chase duration after favorable inflation data. The unchanged long bond left 2s30s 2 basis points steeper at 104; over a month, 30-year yields are still up 18 basis points against a 1-basis-point decline at two years.

Stocks welcomed the prospect of Fed patience, led by technology. Credit markets also remained open: Jane Street placed $14.6 billion of secured bonds, with its longest maturity yielding 8.088%. Access was far less forgiving for The Knot and Air Baltic, whose refinancing plans required higher interest costs or deep creditor losses. CPI eased one source of pressure, while the price of long-term funding and the terms available to weaker borrowers remained demanding.

## Beneath the CPI slowdown, rents and technology prices diverge

The July headline increase followed a 0.4% decline in June. Core inflation picked up from a flat monthly reading to 0.2%, yet its annual rate matched the slowest pace since March 2021. Energy prices fell 1.5%. Shelter increased only 0.1% and accounted for roughly two-thirds of the headline monthly gain, helped by lower hotel and motel prices; both principal rent measures still rose 0.3%.

Services excluding energy and rents increased 0.2% after declining in June, with medical care and airfares among the gains. Goods excluding food and energy rebounded after two monthly declines. Computer software and accessories cost a record 21.2% more than a year earlier, while other computer-related categories recorded their strongest increases in more than four years amid memory-chip shortages and data-center construction. These were pockets of strength within a slower aggregate, rather than evidence of uniformly weak pricing.

Households were not enjoying stronger purchasing power. Real average hourly earnings fell 0.2% from a year earlier, extending weak readings since the Iran conflict began. Together with softer hiring, that gives the Fed a reason to avoid rushing another increase even with headline inflation above 2%. Persistent rents and three dissents at the July meeting nevertheless leave later tightening in play. The market delayed some September risk rather than taking the year-end increase out of prices.

Five-year yields eased 1 basis point to 4.38%. The two-year returned close to its August 7 post-payroll level, while five- and ten-year yields remained above theirs. At ten years, the equal declines in real yields and breakevens differed from Tuesday's entirely breakeven-led rally. Over a month, real yields are still 10 basis points higher and breakevens 2 higher. Most of the accumulated rise in borrowing costs therefore remains after CPI.

The 2s10s curve held at 48 basis points as both yields declined equally. Its monthly steepening of 13 basis points, and the 19-basis-point widening in 2s30s, show how much less relief has reached longer maturities. Ten-year yields remain 12 basis points higher over that period. Deficits, supply and uncertainty about the buyer base did not disappear with one inflation release.

Trading was substantial despite the small closing changes. Nominal-coupon turnover rose 19.7% to $946.1 billion in original-face value. Activity increased 33.4% in maturities of two years or less and 30.9% in seven- to ten-year debt, concentrating the increase around CPI-sensitive notes and the auction sector. The ten-year sale's slight concession was therefore tested in an active market. Thursday's longer auction still has to find its own buyers; the benchmark sale does not settle demand for the much larger duration exposure of a 30-year bond.

## Jane Street raises $14.6 billion as weaker borrowers pay for time

LQD rose 0.12%, HYG 0.13% and JNK 0.17% as Treasuries gained and risk appetite strengthened. Individual transactions gave a more detailed picture of financing conditions, from exceptional secured issuance to restructuring losses.

Jane Street sold $14.6 billion of senior-secured notes, comprising $5.86 billion due in 2031, $5.13 billion in 2033 and $3.64 billion in 2036. The longest tranche yielded 8.088%. Proceeds will refinance floating-rate loans as part of an $11 billion debt overhaul and support technology infrastructure and new trading strategies. Record prior-year trading revenue of $39.6 billion helped support the deal, but investors still required an 8% yield for the longest exposure.

Ratings reflect the unusual combination of profitability and limited balance-sheet transparency. S&P rated the bonds BB, two notches below investment grade; Fitch's issuer rating is BBB-, the lowest investment-grade tier. Secured status and earnings power supported the scale. The cost shows that refinancing and technology spending can obtain substantial capital without obtaining cheap capital.

QTS subsidiaries began investor calls for a potential offering of about $2.85 billion, possibly larger, expected to carry an investment-grade rating. The financing concerns a Blackstone-backed Georgia development leased to Microsoft. It follows discussion of a $5.4 billion bond-and-loan package and July's $3.25 billion leveraged loan backed by Project Magnolia. The latest step is marketing, not a completed sale, as project and asset-backed channels continue to add data-center supply.

Shanghai Electric reopened a more tightly controlled funding route. The city-backed equipment maker priced CNY1.5 billion of three-year green notes in the Shanghai free-trade zone at 1.8%, down from initial discussion around 2.4%. It was the first nonfinancial company to price there since authorities curtailed local-government borrowing in late 2023, and the issuer's first offshore sale since 2020. A Hong Kong subsidiary guarantee, keepwell deed and A3 rating supported demand. The reopening favored a supported, higher-quality borrower rather than reversing the restrictions on local leverage.

The Knot sought much more expensive maturity relief. It launched a $670 million loan to extend an existing $660 million facility by 2.5 years, hours before Moody's cut it two notches to Caa1. The proposed spread is 525 basis points, up from 375, with another 100 basis points if leverage reaches at least four times EBITDA. That increment may be paid in kind. The existing loan had fallen to about 70 cents from roughly 99 late last year.

Revenue fell 2% in 2025 and is expected to decline again in 2026; margins remain in the low-20% range as AI-generated search reduces traffic and vendor engagement. S&P retained a B rating but warned that leverage above seven times earnings could bring a downgrade. Extending maturities gives the business time, while the PIK option preserves cash at the cost of adding debt when leverage is already high.

Air Baltic's secured creditors faced a much deeper impairment. Its €380 million note due in 2029 traded as low as 12 cents on the euro, down from about 35 before the restructuring announcement, although thin trading also produced quotes in the low 20s. The airline plans to exchange much of the note for equity, leave holders with €125 million of debt and raise €225 million of interim financing while reducing fleet size and costs. Its debt-service reserve contained only €3 million in June. Latvia's ownership of 88.4% of the equity and 13% of the bonds has not insulated creditors from losses.

These are different uses of the capital markets, not variations on one broad credit move. Jane Street refinances and expands at a high coupon; QTS tests another infrastructure financing; Shanghai Electric accesses a regulated offshore-yuan channel. The Knot and Air Baltic instead seek time and balance-sheet relief, with existing creditors bearing more of the cost.

## Korean long yields hit a record as Japan debates the pace of tightening

Korea's 30-year government-bond yield reached 4.67%, its highest since the maturity was introduced in 2012. Imported energy costs and warnings that semiconductor-led growth could require more tightening had already pressured the curve. Weak demand from life insurers added a distinct problem at the long end. Officials may reduce ultra-long issuance to below 30% of next year's program, but that prospective supply adjustment has not prevented a record clearing yield today.

Japan's policy debate continued to complicate yen support. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has repeatedly argued that tighter Bank of Japan policy is central to currency stabilization, while Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has resisted moving so quickly that growth suffers. The BOJ has raised rates twice since she took office, but its rate remains 1%; it also held steady on the day of joint US-Japan intervention. The yen was again approaching 160 per dollar.

Markets expect a possible September or October increase. Takaichi's popularity has weakened as living costs become more prominent, BOJ officials have highlighted upside inflation risks and cabinet members continue to endorse the bank's independence. Bessent is due to meet Governor Kazuo Ueda around the end of August. More consistent policy signals could reduce reliance on repeated intervention. Continued disagreement would leave Japan balancing higher domestic yields against further currency operations, with implications for the relative attraction of Treasuries but no proof of a particular reserve transaction.

Energy remains an external constraint for both markets. The IEA now estimates a global supply shortfall of 1.8 million barrels a day this quarter, more than twice its previous projection, without a durable Hormuz agreement. European power prices face cooling demand from heat and reduced French nuclear generation. Internal UK Treasury modeling put 2026 growth at 0.9% in a worst-case scenario with Hormuz effectively closed through year-end, below March's 1.1% forecast. That is a conditional scenario, not a new realized growth reading.

Higher home-market yields can give foreign institutions alternatives to dollar duration even when US inflation improves. Korea's record long yield is a current price signal; Japan's next rate decision and intervention needs remain uncertain. Together with the enlarged energy deficit, they help explain why a favorable US release need not bring a synchronized global bond rally.

## Indonesia regains buyers; Brazil's election raises the cost of carry

The dollar reversed its initial CPI decline to finish 0.11% higher at 99.932. A developing-market currency gauge gave up an intraday gain of as much as 0.2% to end little changed in New York. EMB rose 0.12%, but long-duration EM dollar sovereign debt gained only 0.04%. Lower September hike odds helped hard-currency valuations without overwhelming local risks.

The rand gained nearly 0.3% with precious metals, while the real fell 0.3% and the won 0.4%. Brazil's currency has lost almost 2% in August as election concerns grow; Korea remains exposed to energy imports and rising local long yields. EM stocks advanced nonetheless, underscoring that currency weakness was not a uniform rejection of risk.

Indonesia has begun to win buyers back after losing 8.5% this year for dollar-based bond investors, the worst performance in Asia. Earlier concerns over populist spending, central-bank independence and state intervention drove the rupiah to a record low. Destry Damayanti's nomination as Bank Indonesia governor has restored some policy continuity. Plans to scale back the free-meals program and maintain this year's net bond-issuance target, together with S&P's affirmation of the rating and outlook, have helped stabilize confidence.

The benchmark ten-year yield has fallen about 27 basis points from its highest level since 2022. The latest auction drew the strongest bid-to-target ratio since February, and foreign investors were heading for a third consecutive month of net inflows. The next budget still has to substantiate fiscal restraint, and the central bank must support the currency without compromising its mandate. But the improvement now includes both auction demand and returning foreign capital, not just an official assurance.

Brazil's high carry is facing a different test. The real remains about 6% stronger this year, supported by exceptionally high real rates, yet election hedging is light and weekly Treasury auctions have seen weaker demand as local yields rise. Inflation-linked government real yields have climbed above 8%. That attracts investors while making financing expensive for the sovereign, and leaves the currency vulnerable to greater demand for protection before October's presidential election.

Polls strengthening President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's lead revived doubts about whether the next government would deliver a primary surplus sufficient to stabilize debt. Some local managers expect lower short rates but higher long rates, separating room for monetary relief from fiscal concerns. August's currency decline and weak auctions show those concerns entering prices before the election result is known.

EM companies have performed differently from the more vulnerable sovereigns. A broad dollar corporate index's yield fell 19 basis points in August, against just 2 for US corporates, bringing relative borrowing costs to their lowest since January. Oil producers benefiting from the Hormuz closure and distressed issuers making restructuring progress led the move. China Vanke's 2027 bond returned 30% from end-June after a rating upgrade; Gran Tierra Energy's 2031 note gained 18%. Commodity exposure and company-specific recovery explain more here than a common EM rally.

## Technology rallies while gold retains a protection bid

The S&P 500 gained 0.26%, Nasdaq 100 rose 0.74% and semiconductors advanced 2.49%. VIX fell 4.78% to 14.55. Equities treated CPI as room for the Fed to wait rather than as evidence of a sharper growth downturn, with AI enthusiasm keeping the gains concentrated in technology.

WTI slipped 0.90% to $82.45 and Brent 0.66% to $88.32, but remained 9.61% and 11.16% higher over a week. Physical supply had not normalized. Gold rose 2.52% to $4,493.60 even with the firmer dollar and only a 1-basis-point fall in ten-year real yields. Demand for protection therefore persisted alongside risk appetite, rather than following a simple weaker-dollar trade.

Credit funds and EMB posted modest gains, while EM currencies lost their initial lift. The contrast with Air Baltic's restructuring losses and The Knot's punitive refinancing terms makes the broader market's calm more useful as context than as a description of every borrower. CPI supported valuations, but did not erase energy exposure, funding needs or business deterioration.

## Producer prices and the long-bond auction follow CPI

July PPI arrives at 08:30 ET on August 13. Consensus calls for a 0.2% monthly increase after a 0.3% decline, with a 0.1% forecast also in circulation. The categories feeding core PCE, particularly services and trade margins, will show whether CPI's relief extends beyond lower energy and temporary category weakness. A subdued mix would support patience and the two- to five-year sector; broad strength could bring September sensitivity back. Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks later in August will then show how the chair interprets the accumulating evidence.

The same day's $25 billion 30-year auction faces a yield that stayed at 5.24% despite favorable CPI. Its own when-issued level, investor allocations and post-sale trading will be more informative than comparison with the ten-year auction's 4.683% yield. A contained result with broad nondealer demand would show that current yields can attract duration buyers. A tail, heavier dealer retention or renewed steepening would add to evidence that policy-sector relief has not lowered the long end's funding cost.

Hormuz remains unresolved. Sustained vessel passage, accepted terms and lower freight and insurance costs, together with crude below the August 12 closes, would challenge the IEA's enlarged shortfall estimate. Continued closure or new enforcement incidents would leave July CPI's 1.5% energy decline looking backward rather than signaling lasting relief. Whether renewed oil gains also lift breakevens and two-year yields will show how much of that physical disruption is reaching US policy pricing.
